title: Exchange Online Protection (EOP) - Simply Explained

entities.name: Mirko Peters
entities.quote: Welcome to another episode of Microsoft Knowledge Nuggets on M365. FM, I'm Mirko Peters.

entities.name: Exchange Online
entities.quote: Zap is enabled by default for every single exchange online mailbox.

entities.name: Microsoft 365
entities.quote: is the built in email security layer that comes with every Microsoft 365 plan.

quotes.text: EOP is always on, even if you never touch a single setting. You could buy a Microsoft 365 license, never open the admin center. And EOP would still be filtering your email
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes clear that baseline email protection is built in and always active.

quotes.text: EOP does not sandbox unknown files. They can only catch threats that have already been identified.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the critical limitation of signature-based filtering.

quotes.text: If you publish a strict D mark policy for your domain, it becomes much harder for attackers to spoof your company's email addresses.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, actionable recommendation against spoofing.

quotes.text: Business email compromise attacks target the people with authority to move money or approve payments. EOP alone won't stop them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why executives need protection beyond EOP.

quotes.text: Email security isn't a single product you buy and forget about. It's layers that build on each other. Buy what you need but understand the gaps because the gaps are exactly where attackers are looking.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the layered approach to email security.

takeaways: Exchange Online Protection is included in every Microsoft 365 plan and filters spam, known malware and basic phishing through connection filtering, content filtering, signatures and authentication checks.
Zero-hour auto purge retroactively removes messages whose verdict changes after delivery, now also in Teams chats and the Deleted Items folder.
EOP has no sandboxing, click-time link scanning or impersonation protection, so organizations with visible executives should add Defender for Office 365 and publish a strict DMARC record.
hook: Every Microsoft 365 tenant already has email protection, but few admins know where it stops. This episode breaks down Exchange Online Protection's three filtering layers, the zero-hour auto purge safety net and the gaps attackers exploit. Small and mid-sized businesses learn when EOP is enough and when Defender for Office 365 is worth the upgrade.
